s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic vision disturbance with signs of intraocular inflammation and macular edema
salient_findings: Cystoid macular edema with subfoveal fluid
Keratic precipitates and cells in the anterior chamber
key_facts: Blurry vision in right eye for several months
Anastrozole therapy for more than 2 years
Conjunctival injection and fine keratic precipitates in right eye
Cystoid macular edema with yellow spot in fovea in right eye
No peripheral inflammation in either eye
Normal blood tests for vasculitis and rheumatologic disorders

shortlist.why_kept: History of bilateral iritis and presence of fine keratic precipitates

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Cystoid macular edema and history of bilateral iritis

raw.rationale: The patient's history of recurrent bilateral iritis, presence of fine keratic precipitates, and cystoid macular edema are consistent with Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis. The lack of systemic symptoms and normal blood tests for vasculitis and rheumatologic disorders also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Normal blood tests and lack of systemic symptoms make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with focal retinochoroiditis, which is not described in the vignette

rejected.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with granulomatous uveitis and systemic symptoms, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Sympathetic ophthalmia
rejected.why: Typically occurs after penetrating eye injury, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Multifocal choroiditis and panuveitis
rejected.why: Typically presents with multiple choroidal lesions and vitritis, which are not described in the vignette

rejected.label: Birdshot chorioretinopathy
rejected.why: Typically presents with characteristic birdshot lesions in the retina, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Herpes simplex iridocyclitis
rejected.why: Typically presents with recurrent episodes of uveitis and keratitis, but the vignette does not provide evidence of herpes simplex infection
